These routes of the platform API come from its [OpenAPI document](../openapi.json); [The REST API as a contract](../rest-api.md) says what Lakana promises about them.

## `GET /api/v1/sign-in/session`

Describe your browser session

Answers who is signed in, until when step-up actions need no new passkey touch, and whether a passkey must or may be registered now. A request with a token gets 409: a token has no session. Answers 409 while the web interface is off.

Parameters:

| Name | In | Required | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `authorization` | header | no | text or null | The credential: `Bearer <token>` with a personal access token, task token or CI token. Without it, the web interface's session cookie counts instead. |

Answers:

| Status | Meaning | Body |
|---|---|---|
| `200` | Successful Response | `SessionOut` |
| `401` | Not signed in: the token or browser session is missing, wrong, expired or revoked; an ended session says why in `reason`. | `ErrorOut` |
| `409` | The request conflicts with the current state; the message says what to change. | `ErrorOut` |
| `422` | Validation Error | `HTTPValidationError` |

Answer fields: `SessionOut`

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | text | yes |  |
| `display_name` | text or null | yes |  |
| `type` | one of `USER`, `SERVICE_ACCOUNT` | yes |  |
| `via` | text | yes |  |
| `step_up_until` | text (date-time) or null | yes |  |
| `needs_passkey` | true or false | yes |  |
| `offer_passkey` | true or false | yes |  |
| `absolute_expires_at` | text (date-time) | yes |  |

## `DELETE /api/v1/sign-in/session`

Sign out

Ends the browser session the request came with, at once, and tells the browser to drop its cookie. A request with a token gets 409: a token has no session to end (revoke the token instead).

Parameters:

| Name | In | Required | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `authorization` | header | no | text or null | The credential: `Bearer <token>` with a personal access token, task token or CI token. Without it, the web interface's session cookie counts instead. |

Answers:

| Status | Meaning | Body |
|---|---|---|
| `204` | Successful Response | none |
| `401` | Not signed in: the token or browser session is missing, wrong, expired or revoked; an ended session says why in `reason`. | `ErrorOut` |
| `409` | The request conflicts with the current state; the message says what to change. | `ErrorOut` |
| `422` | Validation Error | `HTTPValidationError` |

## `POST /api/v1/sign-in/links/describe`

Describe a sign-in link before it is used

Needs no credential and never uses the link: the sign-in page shows "Sign in as X" (or "Join as X") from this, so a link preview or a mail scanner opening the page cannot use it. Takes only the public id (`l=` after the `#`), never the secret. A used, expired, withdrawn or unknown link answers 410 with `state` and what to do next.

Request body (application/json, required): `LinkIdIn`

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `link_id` | text | yes |  |

Answers:

| Status | Meaning | Body |
|---|---|---|
| `200` | Successful Response | `LinkDescriptionOut` |
| `409` | The request conflicts with the current state; the message says what to change. | `ErrorOut` |
| `403` | Signed in, but not allowed to do this; the message says why and what to do next. | `ErrorOut` |
| `410` | The sign-in link cannot be used: `state` says whether it was used, expired, withdrawn or is not known; ask for a new link. | `ErrorOut` |
| `422` | Validation Error | `HTTPValidationError` |

Answer fields: `LinkDescriptionOut`

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `kind` | text | yes |  |
| `name` | text | yes |  |
| `display_name` | text or null | yes |  |
| `state` | text | yes |  |

## `POST /api/v1/sign-in/links/redeem`

Sign in with a link

Needs no credential: the link is the proof, and it works once. Starts a browser session with a fresh id (a session the browser had is ended) and sets its cookie. An invite creates the account first, with no rights. After a setup, invite or recovery link on an account without a passkey, `needs_passkey` is true: register one now. After a local link `offer_passkey` may be true instead. A local link is not used while the browser is signed in (409); a used, expired, withdrawn or unknown link, or a wrong secret, answers 410 with `state`.

Request body (application/json, required): `LinkRedeemIn`

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `link_id` | text | yes |  |
| `secret` | text | yes |  |

Answers:

| Status | Meaning | Body |
|---|---|---|
| `200` | Successful Response | `SignInOut` |
| `409` | The request conflicts with the current state; the message says what to change. | `ErrorOut` |
| `403` | Signed in, but not allowed to do this; the message says why and what to do next. | `ErrorOut` |
| `410` | The sign-in link cannot be used: `state` says whether it was used, expired, withdrawn or is not known; ask for a new link. | `ErrorOut` |
| `422` | Validation Error | `HTTPValidationError` |

Answer fields: `SignInOut`

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | text | yes |  |
| `needs_passkey` | true or false | yes |  |
| `offer_passkey` | true or false | yes |  |
| `csrf_token` | text | yes |  |

## `POST /api/v1/sign-in/setup-link`

Issue the setup link that signs the first administrator in

Only the server operator's bootstrap token (the one the server wrote to `LAKANA_BOOTSTRAP_TOKEN_FILE` or was given) may ask, and only while the first administrator has no passkey; afterwards 409 names a recovery link instead. The link works once, for 10 minutes; earlier open setup links are withdrawn.

Answers:

| `409` | The request conflicts with the current state; the message says what to change. | `ErrorOut` |
| `401` | Not signed in: the token or browser session is missing, wrong, expired or revoked; an ended session says why in `reason`. | `ErrorOut` |
| `403` | Signed in, but not allowed to do this; the message says why and what to do next. | `ErrorOut` |
| `422` | Validation Error | `HTTPValidationError` |

Answer fields: `IssuedLinkOut`

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `url` | text | yes |  |
| `expires_at` | text (date-time) | yes |  |

## `POST /api/v1/sign-in/local-link`

Issue a sign-in link for yourself, with your own token, on your own machine

Only while local sign-in is on (`LAKANA_UI__LOCAL_SIGN_IN`, which `lakana server start --local` sets; 404 otherwise), only with a person's own personal access token (never a task, CI or service-account token, and never a browser session). The link works once, for 60 seconds (the start opens it in the browser at once), signs in without a passkey touch, and its session ends when the token is revoked.

Parameters:

| Name | In | Required | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `authorization` | header | no | text or null | The credential: `Bearer <token>` with a personal access token, task token or CI token. Without it, the web interface's session cookie counts instead. |

| `401` | Not signed in: the token or browser session is missing, wrong, expired or revoked; an ended session says why in `reason`. | `ErrorOut` |
| `403` | Signed in, but not allowed to do this; the message says why and what to do next. | `ErrorOut` |
| `404` | What the request names does not exist, or the caller may not know that it does. | `ErrorOut` |
| `422` | Validation Error | `HTTPValidationError` |

Answer fields: `IssuedLinkOut`

## `POST /api/v1/sign-in/step-up/options`

Start confirming your browser session with a passkey touch (step-up)

Some actions in the web interface need a passkey touch no older than 15 minutes, such as adding or removing a passkey, issuing invites and recovery links and ending other people's sessions; without one they answer 403 `StepUpRequired`. The options list your own passkeys. An account with no passkey at this address gets 409 `NoPasskeyError`: add a passkey on your account page first. A token has no browser session, so it gets 409: step-up never applies to a token's requests.

Parameters:

| Name | In | Required | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `authorization` | header | no | text or null | The credential: `Bearer <token>` with a personal access token, task token or CI token. Without it, the web interface's session cookie counts instead. |

Answers:

| Status | Meaning | Body |
|---|---|---|
| `200` | Successful Response | `PasskeyOptionsOut` |
| `409` | The request conflicts with the current state; the message says what to change. | `ErrorOut` |
| `401` | Not signed in: the token or browser session is missing, wrong, expired or revoked; an ended session says why in `reason`. | `ErrorOut` |
| `422` | Validation Error | `HTTPValidationError` |

Answer fields: `PasskeyOptionsOut`

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ceremony_id` | text (uuid) | yes |  |
| `public_key` | mapping of text to any | yes |  |

## `POST /api/v1/sign-in/step-up`

Confirm your browser session with a touch of one of your passkeys

Send the browser's `credential.toJSON()` for the ceremony `/step-up/options` started. Only a passkey of the account the session is signed in as counts; another person's, an answer from another address or without user verification, or a used or expired challenge answers 403 `PasskeyRefused` and the session stays as it was.

Parameters:

| Name | In | Required | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `authorization` | header | no | text or null | The credential: `Bearer <token>` with a personal access token, task token or CI token. Without it, the web interface's session cookie counts instead. |

Request body (application/json, required): `PasskeyAnswerIn`

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ceremony_id` | text (uuid) | yes |  |
| `credential` | mapping of text to any | yes |  |

Answers:

| Status | Meaning | Body |
|---|---|---|
| `200` | Successful Response | `StepUpOut` |
| `409` | The request conflicts with the current state; the message says what to change. | `ErrorOut` |
| `401` | Not signed in: the token or browser session is missing, wrong, expired or revoked; an ended session says why in `reason`. | `ErrorOut` |
| `403` | Signed in, but not allowed to do this; the message says why and what to do next. | `ErrorOut` |
| `422` | Validation Error | `HTTPValidationError` |

Answer fields: `StepUpOut`

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `step_up_until` | text (date-time) | yes |  |

## `POST /api/v1/sign-in/passkey/options`

Start signing in with a passkey

Needs no credential and no name: the options list no passkeys (`allowCredentials` is empty), so the browser offers the passkeys it has for this address and the person picks one with a touch and a PIN, fingerprint or face. The challenge works once, for 5 minutes. At most `LAKANA_UI__PASSKEY_OPTIONS_PER_IP_PER_MINUTE` (60) calls per client address (IPv6: per /64) and `LAKANA_UI__PASSKEY_OPTIONS_PER_NETWORK_PER_MINUTE` (240) per network (IPv4 /24, IPv6 /48) and minute; past either 429. Nothing is stored for a challenge until it is answered.

Answers:

| Status | Meaning | Body |
|---|---|---|
| `200` | Successful Response | `PasskeyOptionsOut` |
| `409` | The request conflicts with the current state; the message says what to change. | `ErrorOut` |
| `413` | The request body is larger than the server accepts. | `ErrorOut` |
| `429` | Too many attempts from this address; ask again after the time in `Retry-After`. | `ErrorOut` |

Answer fields: `PasskeyOptionsOut`

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ceremony_id` | text (uuid) | yes |  |
| `public_key` | mapping of text to any | yes |  |

## `POST /api/v1/sign-in/passkey`

Sign in with a passkey

Send the browser's `credential.toJSON()` for the ceremony the options route started. A passkey that verifies starts a browser session with a fresh id (a session the browser had is ended), sets its cookie, and counts as a passkey touch for 15 minutes of step-up actions. An unknown, disabled or copied passkey, an answer from another address or without user verification, or a used or expired challenge answers 401 and is recorded in the audit log. A passkey whose signature counter went backwards is disabled (it may have been copied) and the person and every administrator are told.

Request body (application/json, required): `PasskeyAnswerIn`

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ceremony_id` | text (uuid) | yes |  |
| `credential` | mapping of text to any | yes |  |

Answers:

| Status | Meaning | Body |
|---|---|---|
| `200` | Successful Response | `SignInOut` |
| `409` | The request conflicts with the current state; the message says what to change. | `ErrorOut` |
| `413` | The request body is larger than the server accepts. | `ErrorOut` |
| `401` | Not signed in: the token or browser session is missing, wrong, expired or revoked; an ended session says why in `reason`. | `ErrorOut` |
| `422` | Validation Error | `HTTPValidationError` |

Answer fields: `SignInOut`

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | text | yes |  |
| `needs_passkey` | true or false | yes |  |
| `offer_passkey` | true or false | yes |  |
| `csrf_token` | text | yes |  |

## `POST /api/v1/invites`

Invite a new person

Answers the link to send them, shown only here: it works once, for 7 days, and creates their account with no rights; grant roles after you have confirmed who signed up. Needs the ADMIN role and, in a browser, a passkey touch in the last 15 minutes (403 `StepUpRequired`). 409 when a principal (active or not) or another open invite has the name in any letter case, or it is the first administrator's name.

Parameters:

| Name | In | Required | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `authorization` | header | no | text or null | The credential: `Bearer <token>` with a personal access token, task token or CI token. Without it, the web interface's session cookie counts instead. |

Request body (application/json, required): `InviteIn`

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | text | yes |  |
| `display_name` | text or null | no |  |

Answers:

| Status | Meaning | Body |
|---|---|---|
| `201` | Successful Response | `InviteOut` |
| `401` | Not signed in: the token or browser session is missing, wrong, expired or revoked; an ended session says why in `reason`. | `ErrorOut` |
| `403` | Signed in, but not allowed to do this; the message says why and what to do next. | `ErrorOut` |
| `409` | The request conflicts with the current state; the message says what to change. | `ErrorOut` |
| `422` | Validation Error | `HTTPValidationError` |

Answer fields: `InviteOut`

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | text (uuid) | yes |  |
| `name` | text | yes |  |
| `display_name` | text or null | yes |  |
| `url` | text | yes |  |
| `expires_at` | text (date-time) | yes |  |

## `POST /api/v1/principals/{name}/recovery-link`

Issue a recovery link for a person who lost their passkeys

Answers the link to send them, shown only here: it works once, for 1 hour. Using it removes their passkeys, ends their sessions and tells them and every administrator. Needs the ADMIN role and, in a browser, a passkey touch in the last 15 minutes. 403 for anyone who holds or has ever held the ADMIN role, directly or through a group, unless you are the server operator (run `lakana recovery create <name>` with the bootstrap token where the server runs); 409 for yourself (use Add passkey), a service account or a deactivated account.

Parameters:

| Name | In | Required | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | path | yes | text | The person's principal name. |
| `authorization` | header | no | text or null | The credential: `Bearer <token>` with a personal access token, task token or CI token. Without it, the web interface's session cookie counts instead. |

Answers:

| Status | Meaning | Body |
|---|---|---|
| `201` | Successful Response | `RecoveryLinkOut` |
| `401` | Not signed in: the token or browser session is missing, wrong, expired or revoked; an ended session says why in `reason`. | `ErrorOut` |
| `403` | Signed in, but not allowed to do this; the message says why and what to do next. | `ErrorOut` |
| `409` | The request conflicts with the current state; the message says what to change. | `ErrorOut` |
| `404` | What the request names does not exist, or the caller may not know that it does. | `ErrorOut` |
| `422` | Validation Error | `HTTPValidationError` |

Answer fields: `RecoveryLinkOut`

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | text (uuid) | yes |  |
| `name` | text | yes |  |
| `url` | text | yes |  |
| `expires_at` | text (date-time) | yes |  |
